The test image shows a tomato plant pulled from soil with:
- Stem split longitudinally, revealing internal vascular discoloration (yellow/brown)
- White mycelial growth at the stem base near soil line
- Dead/wilted foliage
- Roots visible at top

This strongly suggests **Southern Blight** (white mycelium at soil line + stem rot) or possibly Sclerotinia Timber Rot. Let me check the Southern Blight reference.

The reference shows Southern Blight field damage in sandy soil - consistent with the test image's sandy soil environment. The test image shows a closer view with the characteristic white mycelial mat at the stem base (hallmark of Sclerotium rolfsii Southern Blight), and the plant is fully collapsed/dead - matching the field-level wilt pattern in the reference.

The white cottony growth at the soil line on the stem, combined with the sandy soil and complete plant death, is the classic presentation of Southern Blight.
